Shri A.S. Baghel -Government Advocate for respondent/Sta
 Order

This is the sixth application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.495 of 2021 registered at Police Station Gorabazar District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offences under Sections 363, 366A, 376, 376DA of IPC &
Sections 3/4 & 5l/6 of POCSO Act.

2. In pursuance to the order dated 01.10.2024, Shri Raman Singh Markam, SHO of Police Station Gorabazar District Jabalpur is present before this Court and has submitted that the summons issued by the trial Court have not been received at the police station.
He went to the trial Court and enquired about the same.
The clerk and respective court told him regarding issuance of summons but the same have not been received at the police station.
Therefore, there is a substantial delay.
However, the explanation given by him is found to be unsatisfactory for the simple reason that virtually he is alleging the court regarding the same.
No documents being produced by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50976 2 MCRC-41339-2024 him to substantiate his stand.
3. The counsel appearing for the State submits that he is not having the complete documents with him to enable him to explain whether the summons have been received; he has orally submitted the same.

Under these circumstances, this Court deems it appropriate to direct the concerning trial Court's Judge to look into the matter and conduct an enquiry with respect to the allegation that the summons issued from the trial Court have never been received to the police station, therefore, there is a substantial delay.
The enquiry be conducted and report be submitted for perusal of this Court Shhid Khan vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122797190/

The aforesaid aspect may also be looked into.

4. As far as the present bail application is concerned, it has been filed on the ground of delay in trial pointing out the fact that the applicant is in custody since 10.09.2021 being the sole earning member of the family.
Therefore, the application has been filed.
On earlier occasion, the applicant's bail application registered as MCrC No.18387 of 2022 was dismissed on merits vide order dated 19.04.2022.

Present is the case alleging offence under Sections 363, 366A, 376, 376DA of IPC &
Section 3/4 & 5l/6 of POCSO Act, 2012.

5. It is argued that while disposing of the earlier application being MCrC No.40014 of 2023, the co-ordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 07.11.2023 has fixed the time period of six months for concluding the trial NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:50976 3 MCRC-41339-2024 but the same has not been done.
Therefore, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

6. Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the nature of allegations made against the present applicant, the delay in trial cannot be the sole ground to consider the repeat application for grant of bail.
7. The application is hereby rejected.
However, the trial Court is expected to expedite the proceedings of the trial.
